# Introduction

This Tiny Project analyzes hospital patient data using a sample dataset containing patient names, departments, ages, hospital stay, treatment cost, and satisfaction scores.

# 1. Data Importing

```{r}
patient_data <- read.csv("hospital_patient_data.csv")
patient_data
```

```{r}
head(patient_data)
summary(patient_data)
str(patient_data)
```

# 2. Data Preprocessing and Cleaning

## Checking Missing Values

```{r}
colSums(is.na(patient_data))
```

## Handling Missing Values

```{r}
patient_data$Treatment_Cost[is.na(patient_data$Treatment_Cost)] <- median(patient_data$Treatment_Cost, na.rm=TRUE)
patient_data$Satisfaction_Score[is.na(patient_data$Satisfaction_Score)] <- median(patient_data$Satisfaction_Score, na.rm=TRUE)
```

# 3. Statistical Analysis

```{r}
mean(patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
median(patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
var(patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
sd(patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
min(patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
max(patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
```

# 4. Patients by Department

```{r}
department_count <- table(patient_data$Department)
department_count
```

```{r}
barplot(department_count, main="Number of Patients by Department",
        xlab="Department", ylab="Number of Patients", las=2)
```

# 5. Treatment Cost by Patient

```{r}
barplot(patient_data$Treatment_Cost, names.arg=patient_data$Patient_Name,
        main="Treatment Cost by Patient", xlab="Patient",
        ylab="Treatment Cost", las=2, cex.names=0.7)
```

# 6. Hospital Stay by Patient

```{r}
barplot(patient_data$Stay_Days, names.arg=patient_data$Patient_Name,
        main="Hospital Stay by Patient", xlab="Patient",
        ylab="Stay in Days", las=2, cex.names=0.7)
```

# 7. Satisfaction Score Distribution

```{r}
hist(patient_data$Satisfaction_Score, main="Distribution of Satisfaction Scores",
     xlab="Satisfaction Score", ylab="Frequency")
```

# 8. Age Distribution

```{r}
hist(patient_data$Age, main="Distribution of Patient Age",
     xlab="Age", ylab="Frequency")
```

# 9. Correlation Analysis

## Stay Days and Treatment Cost

```{r}
cor(patient_data$Stay_Days, patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
```

```{r}
plot(patient_data$Stay_Days, patient_data$Treatment_Cost,
     main="Hospital Stay vs Treatment Cost",
     xlab="Hospital Stay (Days)", ylab="Treatment Cost", pch=19)
```

## Age and Treatment Cost

```{r}
cor(patient_data$Age, patient_data$Treatment_Cost)
```

```{r}
plot(patient_data$Age, patient_data$Treatment_Cost,
     main="Age vs Treatment Cost",
     xlab="Age", ylab="Treatment Cost", pch=19)
```

# 10. Findings

- Patient data was analyzed using age, hospital stay, treatment cost, and satisfaction score.
- Patients were compared across departments.
- Treatment costs and hospital stays were represented using bar plots.
- Age and satisfaction score distributions were examined using histograms.
- Correlation analysis was used to examine relationships between hospital stay, age, and treatment cost.

# 11. Conclusion

The Hospital Patient Analysis project demonstrates how R can be used to import, clean, analyze, and visualize healthcare-related data using statistical calculations, graphs, and correlation analysis.
